text:
ConocoPhillips fell slightly today as oil prices retreated on hopes for diplomatic resolution in the Middle East. Crude prices dropped after days of sharp gains driven by Houthi attacks on Saudi facilities and shipping in the Strait of Hormuz; traders appear to be pricing in a potential de-escalation, which would ease supply concerns that had pushed oil higher. The stock had surged 11.77% over the past two weeks on the back of those geopolitical tensions, so today's small decline is a modest pullback from that rally.

The gap between U.S. oil ($101.91/barrel) and global oil ($126.55/barrel) remains wide, reflecting ongoing Middle East risk premiums that continue to support energy stocks even as immediate tension eases. Any actual diplomatic breakthrough would likely extend today's downward pressure, while renewed attacks would reverse it quickly.
